events.title: Trump has arrived in Asia. Here’s what he said about Iran and Deutsche Bank
events.summary: Trump has arrived in Manila ahead of meetings with regional leaders and a trip to China for talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin. He threatened Iran after CNN reported a possible dirty bomb or chemical weapon plot in Washington, D.C. Trump said Deutsche Bank “shouldn’t have” leaked his tax details, after the FT reported the bank mistakenly disclosed them in 2017 and didn't tell the White House. U.S. President Donald Trump has arrived for his high-stakes trip to Asia, and took a range of questions on subjects from Iran to Deutsche Bank leaking details about his tax. The president landed in Manila, Philippines, for the initial leg of his trip on Tuesday and answered rapid-fire questions from the press while meeting with other leaders. Asked about a possible Iranian threat to Washington, D.C., he said that, if there were an attack, Iran would "pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before." The question was about CNN reporting that U.S. intelligence suggested the country was planning to target senior members of Trump's administration with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon in the U.S. capital. "We take it very seriously because they happen to be crazy," Trump said. CNBC has not independently verified CNN's report. But the president also said he believed his administration was "very close to getting it done" when it came to the Iran war. While Trump was airborne, the Financial Times reported Deutsche Bank had mistakenly leaked details of his taxes in March 2017, during his first presidential term. The mistake was kept from the White House at the time, according to the FT. In a statement, Deutsche Bank said the issues detailed in Tuesday's media reports go back many years. "Where relevant, we reviewed these matters at the time and worked closely with regulators," the lender said. Asked about the situation in Manila, the president said, "I paid a lot of tax." "They shouldn't have done it. It's illegal for them to do it," he added. Trump was also asked about Nvidia 's announcement on Tuesday of a new National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee. The company, which reports earnings later on Tuesday, is reeling from the sudden departure of CEO Jensen Huang , who resigned last week after having an affair with a woman U.S. intelligence reportedly believes to be a Chinese spy. "It's a great company. It's a great idea," Trump said. Trump is due to fly to Shenzhen, China, where he is scheduled to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a three-way meeting on Thursday, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. He is also due to hold a separate bilateral meeting with Xi. Asked by a reporter if he would have a separate meeting with only Putin, Trump said: "I don't know, but I would, if it's available, I would do that. He's coming. I mean, it's really with the guests. I am the guest of President Xi." Trump met the leaders of Australia, India and Japan as part of the Quad grouping in the Philippines and the prime minister of Thailand. He is due to China on Wednesday. Speaking at a dinner with Southeast Asian leaders as the event wrapped up for the day, Trump touted his record during his second term, citing investment into the U.S., trade deals made with countries represented by attendees at the dinner, energy infrastructure buildouts and America's AI industry. Trump, who has led a campaign to rename artificial intelligence "super intelligence," or "SI," told leaders around the table that the U.S. is "leading the world" in the technology. "We have the world's most powerful SI ecosystem," he said. "We're leading everybody by a lot, and we hope to keep it that way, and we will keep it that way." He added that the U.S. has "the strongest and most capable military on the planet," pointing to investments in the armed forces and the country's defense sector. "We make the greatest equipment. You saw that in Venezuela. You see it in Iran. You see it everywhere," Trump said.

events.title: More than 100,000 take part in France pay protests
events.summary: Government says 146,000 take part in rallies across France, as CGT trade union put the nationwide total over 500,000. More than 100,000 people have taken to the streets in France to protest against the high cost of living, with public sector workers demanding pay increases. The Interior Ministry said on Tuesday that a total of 146,000 people took part in the protests, with 28,000 in Paris alone. The CGT trade union put the nationwide total at just over 500,000 demonstrators. list 1 of 3 Young French students who see ‘no change’ keep up protests in Paris suburbs list 2 of 3 Why are Europe’s governments struggling to respond to growing protests? list 3 of 3 France summons Iran’s ambassador over supermarket fridge ‘sabotage’ Several trade unions had called for a day of strike action. Participants included public sector workers, as well as school pupils and university students. France’s 5.8 million public sector employees were pushed to mobilise after talks with Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu on Friday failed to satisfy union demands. Union representatives left the meeting organised by Lecornu saying the proposed measures failed to address the urgency of the pay situation. Tuesday’s rally is the third call for a united day of action and strikes in the public sector since September. Unions have been pushing for across-the-board pay rises since last week’s boost to the minimum wage for private-sector workers. Protesters say “they simply can’t make ends meet, and they want the government to help them put more money into funding in terms of salaries, in terms of raising the minimum wage”, Al Jazeera’s Natacha Butler reported from Paris. “The government’s already offered about $30 extra a month on the minimum wage, but those here say that is simply not enough. With inflation, with the way the prices are going up, they say they actually need more.” The unions put the loss of purchasing power for public servants at 16 percent since 2017, leading to increasing numbers of public employees ending up on or close to the minimum wage against a backdrop of inflation. “The government doesn’t have much margin or wiggle room financially , because of France’s ballooning debt, and the government’s in the middle of trying to push through a budget with cost-cutting measures in it,” Butler said. Public-sector workers aim to pressure the government to unfreeze the pay scale point used to calculate their basic salary. However, the government has ruled out any general pay rise for the fourth consecutive year in its draft budget. “The people in the street know there is only so far you can go; the government knows they do not have a lot of economic wiggle room. Yet nobody really is coming up with another solution,” Butler said. Despite the government’s efforts to ease tensions, demonstrations have roiled the country for over a month. Student-led protests demanding better conditions in education erupted in mid-September, but the movement has since expanded in scope to cover a range of issues, from high fuel prices to wages and social housing Protests for higher wages, lower costs of living and better public services have also spread across Europe.

events.title: Jensen Huang breaks his silence. Read the statement.
events.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Soeren Stache/picture alliance via Getty Images Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang broke his silence on Tuesday. Huang said he would be "honored" to return to Nvidia. Nvidia's board has said it is not currently considering reinstating Huang. Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said he would be "honored" to return to Nvidia if its board decides it's in the company's best interest. In a statement, Huang again acknowledged making "serious mistakes in my personal life," and said he would cooperate with the board's independent investigation. Nvidia's board is not currently considering reinstating Huang , according to a person familiar with the board's thinking, despite mounting support for his return both inside and outside of the company. It's the first public declaration Huang has made signaling his desire to return to the company he cofounded 33 years ago. A spokesperson for Nvidia declined to comment. "Over the past week, I've been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met," Huang said in the statement. An online petition has garnered more than 190,000 signatures and employees have also supported Huang's reinstatement inside the company with internal posts. Huang resigned last Thursday after admitting to infidelity. The board is investigating whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort . CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO while the company searches for a permanent successor. Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1 about what he knew about former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang and other potential export-control issues. Nvidia has also formed a new special committee to oversee exports and national security as scrutiny has intensified over the flow of the company's chips to China. On Monday, the Commerce Department issued new rules that tightened remote access to advanced chips. Nvidia reports its quarterly earnings today — the first time since his departure from the company. He ended the statement with a message to his family . "I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours." Read Huang's statement in full below: Over the past week, I've been overwhelmed by the love and support of friends, industry colleagues, and people I've never met. Thank you to everyone who has shown kindness to my family and me. It means the world to me. I came to the United States 53 years ago, and becoming an American citizen is one of the greatest gifts and proudest moments of my life. NVIDIA has been my life's work. Building it into the company it is today alongside my colleagues has been a privilege and an honor. Nowhere but in America could a company like NVIDIA be possible. I love our country, and I love NVIDIA. I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life. I created problems for the Board that I deeply regret. I own my mistakes completely, and I am committed to cooperating with the Board's independent investigation. Since my departure, I've seen an outpouring of calls from NVIDIA's employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO. Many continue to reach out to me directly as the company navigates complex technology, market, competitive, and geopolitical dynamics. NVIDIA is a once-in-a-generation company. If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO. Thank you again to everyone who has shared their good wishes. I am profoundly humbled by your support. To my family: I love you, and I will spend the rest of my life being worthy of yours. events.title: US-China AI race causing global ‘alarm,’ UN's top tech enovy says
events.summary: The rest of the world is looking at the AI arms race between the US and China with “some kind of alarm,” the UN’s top tech envoy said Tuesday. Other countries “don’t want their agency taken away with this attention just on this competition between two players,” Amandeep Singh Gill, the Under-Secretary-General and Special Envoy for Digital and Emerging Technologies of the United Nations, said at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World. “The rest of the world wants to build up its own models, its own infrastructure.” Gill told Semafor’s Mohammed Sergie that while other countries are not trying to compete with frontier labs in the US and China, they still want to innovate. “So this also translates to some alarm in terms of guardrails, because if you have a race, then you tend to ignore the rules,” Gill said, adding that recent incidents around AI safety have sparked concerns among several countries that “shortcuts are being taken.” Building out Africa’s AI infrastructure Gill also emphasized the importance of addressing Africa’s AI shortfall, saying more capacity needs to be built to bridge the AI divide and guarantee the continent access to emerging technologies. Gill said a country like Ethiopia, with a population above 130 million, needs significantly more GPUs. “You need a massive infusion of capacity, but capacity alone is not enough,” he added. Connectivity and energy availability are necessary, too. Investing in African AI would be “creating a market,” Gill said, and could improve AI’s reputation by showing how it can be used to improve water scarcity, public health, and public services issues. “It’s easy to say AI will solve cancer, but if you can point to these useful applications that work at societal scale, then it reinforces the case on the beneficial side of AI,” Gill added. — Ben Kesslen

events.title: Salesforce sets AI budgets after employees spent 'thousands of dollars per month on tokens,' memo says
events.summary: Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff. Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images Salesforce is setting AI budgets for employees. Some spent thousands per month on tokens last quarter, according to an internal memo. Other companies have introduced similar spending limits to rein in climbing AI costs. Salesforce is setting AI budgets for employees after some spent thousands per month on tokens last quarter, according to an internal memo viewed by Business Insider. "Starting this month, every role has a monthly token budget, so we can focus our AI spend on the work that matters most for our customers and business," Salesforce Chief Operating Officer Miguel Milano wrote in an email to employees. The budgets reflect a delicate balance for companies adopting AI. They want to control spending for the expensive technology without discouraging employees from using it. A Salesforce spokesperson said the company does not have companywide individual token budgets, leaving it up to team leaders to manage AI usage. "Our focus is always to ensure that our AI investments deliver the greatest impact for our business and customers," the spokesperson added. Salesforce piloted the new AI budgets on one team for a month and found that group "was operating well under budget by month two with no drop in output," the memo stated. The sales organization under President and Chief Revenue Officer Alexa Vignone will have a budget of $1,000 per month for technical roles, and $100 per month for non-technical roles like sellers. Salesforce Customer Success, under Jim Roth, and Salesforce Global Professional Services and Forward Deployed Engineering, under Lori Steele, will have budgets of $500 per month for technical roles and $100 per month for non-technical roles. Other companies have introduced similar spending limits. As Business Insider recently reported , Coinbase has weekly AI spending caps ranging from $500 to $5,000 based on employee roles and seniority. JPMorgan Chase introduced a $2,000 monthly limit for some engineers using Anthropic's Claude Code. In May, Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff said the company expected to spend roughly $300 million on Anthropic tokens this year, largely for coding agents. Read the memo Team, As we scale our AI capabilities, we're getting smarter about how we manage them. Last quarter, some individuals spent thousands of dollars per month on tokens. With AI confidence now high, we're shifting focus from adoption to impact. Starting this month, every role has a monthly token budget, so we can focus our AI spend on the work that matters most for our customers and business. OU leaders will manage each of their team's budgets, similar to T&E, so one person's spike can be offset by others. Starting next week, when an individual's Al spend is approaching 100%, the individual and the manager will both get a notification from the DevBar app in Slack, with the option to request advanced approval up to 20% above the individual limit. When an individual's spend is approaching 100%, the individual and the manager will both get a Slack notification from the DevBar app, with the option to request advanced approval up to 20% above the individual limit. If you or your team needs more budget, request exceptions. Approval needs scale with the size of the ask: Up to 20% above the individual limit, one-time request: the second line manager approves. More than 20% above, up to 3x the individual limit: the third line manager approves, and you'll need to include an ROI justification. The increase lasts 90 days and is reviewed when it expires. Above 3x the individual limit: Alexa, Jim, or Lori to approve, with finance. These are reviewed every month. We never want a budget to get in the way of great work: if you have a high-impact use case that needs more, ask. Sellers, try Slack Surfaces or Claude Artifacts. Even heavy users typically spend <$100 per month. More token budget management resources are coming soon. For now, go to the Al Tools Optimization canvas for DevBar setup, model-to-task guidance, and FAQs. Why I'm confident: We piloted this in T&P, and after a hands-on first month, the team was operating well under budget by month two with no drop in output. events.title: Scammers are sending fake emails to people worried about Nvidia's stock
events.summary: Scammers are already exploiting the scandal surrounding Nvidia to lure unsuspecting investors and business professionals into downloading malware. Why it matters: AI is making it easier for criminals to capitalize on the news cycle and tailor scams to specific audiences before people have time to recognize the threat. Driving the news: KnowBe4, the cybersecurity training platform, says it's seen scammer emails using the subject line "Invitation: Nvidia Executive Partnership Discussion" that purport to offer information about Nvidia's investment strategy. Inside the email, recipients see a clickable image appearing to show information about Nvidia's 2026 investment parameters. Clicking it could lead to malware being downloaded onto their devices. KnowBe4 started seeing signs of the scam Wednesday, just a few days after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and a day before he resigned, triggering a crisis at the chip-maker. KnowBe4 CEO Bryan Palma told Axios that the campaign appears to be targeting people working in finance, transportation and government. It's unclear which group is behind the emails, he added. The big picture: The Nvidia lure is part of a growing trend in which hackers borrow a page from the marketing industry's playbook to turn breaking news into targeted phishing campaigns. Just like marketers, hackers can purchase detailed contact lists and use AI to sort potential victims by industry, profession and interests, Palma said. That allows them to tailor their scams to specific audiences rather than sending the same generic email to millions of people. AI is also speeding up their ability to develop and launch timely schemes, Palma said. By the numbers: Attackers are 5.4 times faster at responding to headlines in 2026 than in 2022, according to KnowBe4 data . In one case, following a major celebrity's death, scammers launched an email phishing campaign within 16 hours. Nearly 88% of phishing attacks tied to breaking news or planned events impersonated a globally recognized brand, according to KnowBe4. The bottom line: Palma recommends taking a closer look at any unexpected email that appears to reference breaking news, even if the headline seems familiar.

events.title: Anthropic forges ahead with its IPO even as AI fears mount and markets wobble
events.summary: Anthropic is preparing to sell stock to the public in a shaky moment for artificial intelligence companies NEW YORK -- Investors fearing an AI bubble are getting jittery. Financing costs are rising. Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry. It's not an ideal time for an artificial intelligence company to sell stock, but Anthropic is pressing ahead with its blockbuster initial public offering anyway. No ordinary sale, the Claude chatbot maker's IPO could raise more than $60 billion on Thursday, a massive haul that, depending on the ultimate pricing and other issues, could rival SpaceX's in June . But Anthropic is facing headwinds as it prepares for its coming-out party . Tech stocks have done well so far this year, but the path higher has been rocky, especially for AI-related companies. That's not a reassuring setup for the IPO. One particularly volatile AI stock, CoreWeave, plunged 15.5% on Oct. 14 over fears it wouldn't be able to borrow enough, cheaply enough to fund its growth. The stock then swung wildly. On Wednesday, the company, which buys chips and then rents out access to them to customers over the cloud, surged 25% after an encouraging earnings report, only to plunge 7% the next day. Most stocks move no more than 2% on the average trading day. Adding to the sector volatility recently has been the abrupt departure of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang over extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Huang, a high-profile AI booster, built Nvidia into a linchpin of the industry and a major financial backer of other AI companies. Stock in the AI chip designer dropped 4% Monday, dragging the broader S & P 500 down for a third day in a row. Nvidia has agreed to buy an estimated $10 billion of Anthropic stock after the IPO. It also sells chips to Anthropic but the latter also buys from AMD and others. As to whether the gyration in AI-tied stocks argues for an IPO delay, note that volatility can cut both ways: It might be signaling the much debated AI bubble could burst soon so it's better to sell stock now, fast. And history shows demand for IPOs can disappear quickly. In 2021, nearly 400 companies went public in the U.S., but then investors got scared of a possible recession the next year and demand dried up with only 71 making market debuts. Another reason to sell stock now is that the other way to raise money — borrowing — has gotten more expensive. That's partly due to inflation fears and partly due to the sector’s massive cash needs, which have drawn comparisons to the Gilded Age splurge on railroads. Lenders fear AI companies have taken on too much debt to expand while having no clear path to profitability. Anthropic already has taken on $6.2 billion in debt, which it acknowledges in financial filings is “substantial." Adding to the strain, the company is unprofitable, at least under standard accounting rules, suggesting its resources are limited to pay interest and principal. Whipped cream sold at Costco in 12 states voluntarily recalled Authorities investigate 'credible' unknown device threat at Illinois plant Nationwide ground stop lifted after more than 4 hours; officials blame old tech On the plus side, it has ample cash, although it will likely run through it quickly if it can't raise more soon given its outsized spending plans. The company said it has already signed leases and other deals requiring it to spend $900 billion in computing and infrastructure in the coming years, including $70 billion in the next 12 months. Higher interest rates are not the only problem. Politics threatens to slow growth, too. Newly elected Democrats are vowing to crack down on the industry amid a national backlash against data centers, giving new impetus to a Congressional effort last year to enact a national moratorium on new ones. And two big states offering incentives for data centers, Texas and Georgia, just elected Democrat governors vowing to stop new construction. It wouldn't be unprecedented for Anthropic to postpone its IPO at the last minute. After a bout of volatility following President Donald Trump’s “Liberation Day” tariffs in April 2025, several companies postponed their initial offerings, including the online ticket marketplace StubHub and Klarna, a buy now, pay later business. And an Australian data center company, Firmus, called off its IPO last month because of jitters in the market. But newly elected Democrats don't take office until January. Anthropic could be betting that selling now is best before the feared crackdown begins in earnest. If the company does go ahead as expected, it will beat rival OpenAI to the market. That's an important advantage should investors suddenly fear they have too much exposure to the sector and decide they don't want to buy stock in the next public AI company. And despite the jitters, companies on public markets are still fetching top prices. One measure of investor enthusiasm shows they are paying nearly as much as ever to buy stocks.

events.title: Verizon is ready to 'ferociously compete' with Musk as billionaire muscles into telecom
events.summary: Verizon CEO Dan Schulman said Tuesday he’s ready to “ferociously compete” against SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, who is muscling his way into the telecom industry and looking at scooping up wireless businesses to build out a ground network. Schulman said at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World that Musk hasn’t yet called him to formally broach a deal, and that he’d prefer to go at it alone, but that if the billionaire called him he would be “happy to talk.” Musk declared last month SpaceX would “ become a major mobile carrier in the US ,” sending shares of Verizon plunging — wiping out $50 billion across the three major US telecoms operators in a single day. “It’s hard to punch at something that doesn’t exist” and “it’s hard to build a terrestrial network in under four or five years,” Schulman said, joining his fellow telecom CEOs in pushing back on the idea that SpaceX would be able to compete in the hardware-intensive legacy business. “When he finally spends $300 billion building that out, he’ll have a network that looks very much like the networks of most of the mobile network operators. And four years from now, we will be at least two generations beyond where we are today.” Verizon is overlaying AI infrastructure across its network, and plans to bundle AI services to sell to consumers, he added. — Kelsey Warner

events.title: Nvidia tells robotics startups they have its support as questions swirl about its investment strategy
events.summary: Nvidia's headquarters. Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images Nvidia reassured robotics startups that its support would remain after Jensen Huang’s exit. Interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to pursue deals more slowly than Huang. Nvidia has backed more than 35 robotics and physical AI companies. Nvidia is reaching out to robotics startups with a message after Jensen Huang's sudden departure: The chipmaker still has their backs. Since Huang's resignation, the company and its venture capital arm, NVentures, have contacted at least three robotics startups they back to reassure them of its support, Business Insider has learned. The calls began last Thursday, shortly after Huang's resignation , with startups assured that business would continue as usual. The outreach comes amid uncertainty about Nvidia's broader investment strategy under interim CEO Colette Kress, who is not expected to pursue deals as quickly as Huang and has sometimes pushed back on investments he championed. Nvidia declined to comment on the calls. Under Huang, Nvidia became a major backer of robotics and "physical AI," the term he popularized for AI that can act in the real world. At the company's conferences, he often appeared onstage flanked by humanoid robots. Huang described robotics as the technology industry's "first opportunity to address a $50 trillion industry that has largely been void of technology until now." That enthusiasm translated into investments in more than 35 robotics and physical AI companies, according to PitchBook data. Of these, 29 have disclosed funding rounds totaling nearly $11 billion. Nvidia's portfolio includes humanoid makers Figure AI and Neura Robotics, robot foundation model developer Skild AI , self-driving software company Wayve , and autonomous trucking startup Waabi. The robotics investments are part of a broader push that made Nvidia a financial backer of much of the AI ecosystem. At the end of July, it held $48 billion in stakes across 229 private companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic. Nvidia's interim CEO Colette Kress Nvidia Deepu Talla, an Nvidia robotics vice president who worked on some of the company’s investments, told Business Insider that Nvidia intends to "continue to aggressively cultivate the ecosystem.” Nvidia's robotics products brought in $11 billion in the first half of this year, 30% more than in all of 2025, Talla said. Some of that revenue comes from companies Nvidia has invested in. The company's robotics strategy has two parts: developing the simulation tools, software, and chips that power robots, and investing in startups building them. The investments can turn startups into customers while giving Nvidia a stake in their success. "If you look at any cap table of a company that is compute-heavy, Nvidia is probably there, because they knew much of that money was going to flow back to them," one investor whose firm has backed multiple startups alongside Nvidia, told Business Insider. events.title: NSA attributes US network outage to routine ‘maintenance’ activities
events.summary: Can Trump find a way to work with Democrats? Disruption at US intelligence agency comes amid questions over recent outages in air travel, communications services. The United States National Security Agency (NSA) has said an outage affecting its internal communications network was due to “routine maintenance”, following a report by CNN. The report, published on Tuesday and citing six unnamed sources, said there was no evidence that the outage was the result of a cyberattack. The incident follows a series of outages that have gone without explanation in recent days. list 1 of 3 Nationwide ground stop could cost US airlines hundreds of millions list 2 of 3 Why were US banks down? What to know about Chase and Zelle delays list 3 of 3 Democratic lawmakers ask FAA to pause upgrades linked to US ground stop The network, known as NSA Net, allows employees of the US surveillance agency to share highly classified information internally, CNN said. A spokesperson for the NSA downplayed the outage in a statement to Al Jazeera. “The National Security Agency experienced temporary degradation during scheduled routine maintenance,” the statement said. “While some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remain fully operational, and our ability to defend national security continues. NSA’s infrastructure is designed with multiple layers of redundancy to maintain operations during planned maintenance or unexpected events.” The reported network disruption at the NSA follows several other major outages that have affected communication and transportation services in the US. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) temporarily halted all takeoffs in the country on Friday, claiming that a system upgrade caused a flight communication overload. The ground stop, which lasted more than four hours, was called out of an “abundance of caution”, it explained. The tech giant Microsoft also announced that services such as Outlook and Teams were down last week. More recently, on Monday, outages hit major banks, and United Airlines briefly suffered a system disruption that delayed some departing flights. US President Donald Trump has played down the seriousness of those outages. “Things like that happen,” Trump told reporters on Tuesday. “It’s fine.”

events.title: Google expands access to Gemini Tasks, which can help with calls, purchases
events.summary: Google is expanding the rollout of Tasks, a toggle in Gemini that converts the chatbot into a more active helper. Unlike Gemini’s Chat, which merely allows users to talk to Google’s AI assistant for informational purposes, Tasks empowers the app to complete basic secretarial functions, deputizing it as a kind of personal assistant. How, specifically, can you use it? Google says that the app can call businesses and book appointments on users’ behalf; it can also complete purchases for them via Google Pay, and even sign into websites securely if prompted to do so. In a blog post , Josh Woodword, VP of Gemini, claims to have recently used the feature to call local car dealerships to schedule a service appointment for his family’s minivan. He says he also used it to analyze his electrical bill. Tasks was initially launched to select testers back in May as Gemini Spark, a 24/7 agentic helper, and was expanded to U.S. subscribers of its Google AI Ultra tier. Gemini Spark eventually became “Task Mode.” Google is now making the feature available for free to hundreds of millions of people who are using the company’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. Getting the function up and running is easy. Users merely flip a toggle within the app from Chat to Tasks, which enables the feature. Users can also send texts to Gemini or call the app to give it commands. events.title: Nearly $500k of underwater gear in limbo after depot suspended
events.summary: News Home Just In For You Analysis Rural Watch Live Health Indigenous Politics Science Deep Time Elections World Environment Investigations Business Local news Quizzes Sport AFL NRL Football Tennis Cricket Netball Lifestyle Wellbeing Relationships & Family Food & Recipes Personal Finance Home & Garden Entertainment TV & Movies Books Music Pop Culture Arts Goods in limbo after Australian Border Force suspends Top Logistics Australia depot licences Tim Hochgrebe says he has been waiting five months for his goods. ( ABC North Coast: Hannah Ross ) Freight logistics experts say a crackdown on illicit products is slowing supply chains. Businesses awaiting the delivery of imported goods say the delays are creating trade and cash flow problems. Australian Border Force says owners of delayed goods, customs brokers, and freight forwarders should take steps to find to retrieve them. Importer Tim Hochgrebe has almost $500,000 worth of niche underwater equipment languishing somewhere within his supply chain, and no idea how to find it. The Byron Bay-based business owner is dealing with the fallout from the suspension of Top Logistics Australia, a Sydney-based company whose depot licences were cancelled in September by the Australian Border Force (ABF). He is one of a number of small importers left waiting on stock caught up in border delays as the Christmas trade period begins. Company director Peter Ping Xie is due to appear in Burwood Local Court on November 18, charged with dishonestly obtaining financial gain by deception. The ABC has confirmed the charges relate to the alleged importation of illicit tobacco and vapes into Australia. Mr Hochgrebe said the ABF cancellation of Top Logistics Australia had forced his Chinese-based shipping agent to find another freight logistics company in Australia. He said goods he had expected to receive within six weeks had still not arrived five months later. Tim Hochgrebe has been importing goods from China for over a decade. ( ABC North Coast: Hannah Ross ) The company now handling his goods has an email address, but no phone number, and his efforts to contact it have so far failed. "There's no-one we can simply call and say, ' Hey, where's our stuff? Is it going to be a week? Is it going to be a month?'" he said. "It's just the limbo we are in that causes the trouble. "It's starting to affect our cash flow because we don't have the goods we long ago paid for." The ABC understands all consignments held by Top Logistics Australia have been cleared by ABF or transferred to other licensed depots for ongoing storage and processing. ABF recently published Australian Customs Notices advising the owners of goods, customs brokers, and freight forwarders to identify the location of their goods and take steps to retrieve them. The ABC has attempted to contact Top Logistics Australia for comment. Jane Laverty from Business NSW said small businesses were struggling to absorb the cost of delays and refunds, and the hit to their reputations and cash flow. "It's a lot of cost for a small business to be carrying," she said. Logistics experts say supply chains have been disrupted by a crackdown on the illicit tobacco and vape trade. Australian Border Force established Strikeforce Borderdale to tackle trade in illicit tobacco and vapes. ( Supplied: Australian Federal Police ) Industry body Freight and Trade Alliance represents the interests of importers, exporters, freight forwarders and customs brokers in Australia. General manager of freight policy and operations Tom Jensen said there were ongoing delays in the screening of cargo coming through Australian ports, particularly Sydney. Mr Jensen said, since December, border holds on some containers had blown out from one or two days to more than 30 days in extreme cases. "It's one of those things where at the moment a lot of innocent imports are being tied up because their containers are being flagged for inspection," he said. He said any significant delay added extra cost as importers had to pay for storage of the containers at the cargo terminal and container lease fees. Australian Border Force says it is clearing goods through customs within legislated time frames. ( ABC North Coast: Hannah Ross ) "ABF has thrown more resources at this, but there are still significant signs of delays here and there, so it definitely hasn't resolved the situation," he said. Data published in the ABF's 2025/2026 annual report shows sea cargo cleared within five days had fallen from its five-year average by almost 2 per cent, to 91.6 per cent. Victorian-based importer Phil Burn said he had nine remote-control lawn mowers worth $9,000 awaiting customs release. "Due to the excessive delays, I have had to personally refund the purchase cost of every mower," he said. Phil Burn has had to refund his customers due to delivery delays.

events.title: IEEE Celebrates 10 Years of Incorporating Ethics Into AI Systems
events.summary: Policymakers, technologists, and members of the public have raised concerns about the harm AI’s rapid advancement might cause to society. Their concerns include bias, data privacy violations, the spread of misinformation, and losing control of AI agents. Those issues are relatively new to many people, but the IEEE Standards Association has been working for the past decade on ways to prioritize the responsible development of AI systems. In 2016 IEEE SA launched the IEEE Global Initiative for Ethical Considerations in Autonomous and Intelligent Systems (A/IS) and published the Ethically Aligned Design report. EAD ’s mission is to encourage everyone involved in designing autonomous and intelligent systems to prioritize human well-being by applying ethical considerations for the benefit of humanity. Developed by a multidisciplinary community of experts from around the world, the report outlined eight foundational principles for A/IS. They include human rights, people’s well-being, and transparency. More than 100 leading AI ethics experts provided input. EAD ’s Version II report was released in 2017. Both versions solicited public input and received hundreds of pages of feedback, according to John C. Havens , who was the global initiative’s founding executive director, and is now the global director for IEEE Planet Positive 2030 . And by 2019, there were more than 400 contributors and the community continues to grow. “ Ethically Aligned Design was the first of its kind in the sense of a report that was more than a list of principles and from an organization with the credibility of IEEE,” Havens says. “At the time it was released, there wasn’t anything like it.” Since its launch, a series of standards has been developed to provide practical guidelines on designing, building, and deploying technology that prioritizes human values. Several AI ethics certification programs have been introduced. This year marks the 10th anniversary of EAD ’s first draft. To celebrate, IEEE SA recently launched a website , a podcast series , and a blog that reflect on the report’s achievements and impact. Eight guiding principles The word ethics is often used interchangeably with morality , but that is not the case in responsible AI systems design, according to EAD ’s first version. The report includes insights from classical ethics traditions and value-based design methodologies to offer actionable recommendations for engineers developing AI tools. The report established eight foundational general principles for designing autonomous systems: respecting human rights, prioritizing increased well-being as success criteria for development, empowering individuals with data agency to have control over their identity, effectiveness, transparency, accountability, awareness of misuse, and competence for the system creators. The principles shift applied ethics to the design stage of AI systems, compared with being a concern after they’re released, the authors wrote. A suite of standards The IEEE 7000 series of standards has been developed based on EAD ’s framework. Currently the series consists of 29 projects, 11 of which have been published, and more are still being added. They cover topics such as ethical system design model process ( IEEE 7000-2021 ), AI system transparency ( IEEE 7001-2021 ), data privacy ( IEEE 7002-2022 ), algorithmic bias considerations ( IEEE 7003 -2024), the impact on people’s well-being ( IEEE 7010-2020 ), machine-readable personal privacy requirements ( IEEE 7012-2025 ), and systems that mimic human empathy ( IEEE 7014-2024 ). AI ethics certifications IEEE SA offers a suite of ethics in AI programs including IEEE CertifAIEd , which includes two certifications : one for individuals and one for products. The professional certification provides individuals with skills to assess autonomous and intelligent systems for adherence to IEEE’s methodology and ethics criteria. “ Ethically Aligned Design was the first of its kind in the sense of a report that was more than a list of principles and from an organization with the credibility of IEEE.” —John C. Havens, founding executive director of the global initiative The product certification program assesses whether an organization’s AI tool or system conforms to the criteria in the IEEE Ontological Specifications. A CertifiAIEd assessor evaluates the product to ensure it meets the criteria. Upon completion of the assessment, the owner submits it to the IEEE Conformity Assessment Program , which can certify it and issue the certification mark. IEEE SA also recently released its Responsible AI for Children certification program . This program certifies that AI products for children have been independently tested and verified to meet design and ethics requirements. New industry connections group The IEEE Artificial Intelligence Systems (AIS) for Global Flourishing Collaborative Industry Collections group was formed to provide the resources, knowledge, and tools needed to prioritize people’s well-being to developers of AI systems. It has more than 200 members. The collaborative describes its work as a practical, systems-level framework for responsible technology design that translates flourishing into applied methods, metrics, and tools that can be used throughout the AIS lifecycle. The group is establishing guidelines for how to design, evaluate, and govern systems that can measurably improve human well-being and ecological sustainability. Subcommittees are focused on cognition, education, faith, planetary care, spirituality, and other issues. “The group is building directly off the well-being chapter of Ethically Aligned Design and the IEEE 7010 standard (Recommended Practice for Assessing the Impact of Autonomous and Intelligent Systems on Human Well-Being),” Havens says. “That’s on purpose because if human and planetary flourishing aren’t addressed first in design, then human well-being and planetary sustainability are afterthoughts.” Podcasts and blogs To mark the 10-year anniversary, IEEE SA created the five-part “ Ethically Aligned Design : 10 Years of Impact” podcast series . It launched on 21 October. New episodes are being released every two weeks. The episodes center around the vision for EAD , the process for selecting its foundational principles, and how they were translated into the IEEE 7000 standards. The first podcast, “Origins of Ethically Aligned Design,” explored early efforts to make ethics a practical part of AI and autonomous system design. The experts discussed challenges, debates, global collaboration, and the real-world impact that helped move responsible technology from ethical principles toward actionable standards and practices. The second podcast, “The Chapters and Committees” focuses on the multidisciplinary groups that worked on turning broad human values into practical guidance for AI and autonomous systems. events.title: Apple services, including iCloud, App Store, Apple Music, and more, hit by outage
events.summary: After a recent slew of tech outages, service disruptions, and flight chaos this week, now it’s Apple customers who are facing technical issues. The iPhone maker’s System Status page indicates that there are issues with iCloud’s Account & Sign In services affecting “all users,” which could make the service slow or unavailable. The App Store, AppleCare on Device, and Apple Music are also experiencing issues, the page indicates. Like all major tech companies, Apple faces outages and other technical issues affecting its cloud services at times. However, today’s issues are likely more noticeable to end users because problems with iCloud can lead to account sign-in problems. This could cause your iPhone to ask for your Apple ID and password, and you could see other attempts to sign in to services with your Apple account information fail. On Reddit, some folks also noted that they were unable to activate a new iPhone , which is likely related to these ongoing issues. Given the recent increase in AI-driven cyberattacks, users across social media have already begun to speculate about the cause. In particular, users are expressing concerns about the Apple outage, as it arrives only days after technical failures at Microsoft led to its cloud systems that power flagship services like Outlook and Teams failing due to cascading software issues . Similarly, a brief outage of Chase’s banking app this week garnered attention, as did an ongoing partial outage (at the time of publication) of the National Security Agency’s internal classified network, both of which were blamed on software glitches. So far, none of the outages in the past week have been attributed to cyberattacks, but rather to technical problems. Apple has not yet responded to TechCrunch’s request for comment, but it told Bloomberg the outages were caused by an internal update and not a cyberattack. “Many of our systems are back up and running after an internal update caused some outages this morning. We’re working to get the remaining systems online as soon as possible,” the statement read. After the initial outages were reported, Apple’s status page was updated to include other outages impacting Apple School Manager, iCloud Mail, iCloud Web Apps (iCloud.com), Schoolwork, and the Volume Purchase Program. events.title: ‘I’m not afraid of Chinese cars’: GM’s president says Detroit will be the bastion of American manufacturing as China breaks auto export records
events.summary: General Motors President Mark Reuss wanted to make one thing clear at the F500 Innovation Forum in Detroit: “I’m not afraid of Chinese cars.” At the same time, he said GM is taking China’s growing automotive manufacturing industry “very seriously.” China exported more than 8 million passenger vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, and Reuss’ answer is to point to Detroit’s GM’s factories. Reuss spoke during a panel discussion with Fortune ’s Executive Editor Lee Clifford. “I think we do a lot of things really well,” he said. “Core things like safety, durability, reliability, long term, and of course design—aesthetic design.” And the stakes are American jobs: the motor vehicles and component parts sector employed about 2.6 million U.S. workers in 2025, according to the Department of Energy , a drop of more than 50,000 from the year before. But he pointed to GM’s factories, production scale and workforce as competitive advantages that Chinese competitors can’t replicate. “I think Detroit is doing a lot of things well,” he said. “We look at our factories and our scale, and we do scale well.” He also pointed to GM’s people. “I think our talent is second to none. I really do,” Reuss said. “We have the best talent in this country in automotive, I believe.” And one of the ways they were doing it? He said the company had been operating in China since 1984—studying its competitor: “We know Chinese cars,” Reuss said. And GM still takes apart rivals’ cars from around the world to see what competitors are doing, Reuss said. “Only the paranoid survive, right?” China is turning exports into a manufacturing weapon The scale of China’s export growth is hard to ignore. The country exported more than eight million passenger vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, according to the Associated Press —with exports in October alone reaching nearly one million at 927,000, a 62.3% increase from the prior year. And that acceleration follows an already record-setting year—China exported approximately 7.1 million vehicles in 2025, including about 6 million passenger cars. By August 2026, its passenger car exports had already passed the previous year’s total, with shipments jumping 67.1% year over year that month. And a big part of the wave comes from electric vehicles. According to the International Energy Agency, China produced about 16 million electric cars in 2025—which accounts for nearly 75% of global EV production. Its exports more than doubled to a record 2.5 million vehicles, representing more than a third of all Chinese vehicle exports—a 20% rise from 2024. The motor city looks to build its own manufacturing force But the automotive industry is a major part of the manufacturing base in the U.S., supporting millions of jobs across factories, suppliers, distribution networks and repair businesses. And according to a March 2026 Congressional Research Service report, the automotive manufacturing industry accounts for 4.8% of U.S. GDP and supports approximately 10.1 million direct and indirect jobs. Price is part of that fight. GM sells six models priced right around $30,000, Reuss said, and has sold 600,000 of them so far this year, after close to a million last year. “They’re hard to do and make money at it, but we’re on it,” he said. Reuss also said GM learned the hard way that it can’t cut its way out of trouble. For a long stretch, he said, “there wasn’t a year that we didn’t have a reorganization, or downsizing, or consolidation, and it was just exhausting, frankly, for everybody.” GM filed for bankruptcy in 2009. “Nothing happens until you sell a car,” Reuss said. But GM is planning as if tariffs are here to stay. Asked by Clifford whether that holds no matter who is president, Reuss said, “Absolutely.” He added: “It’s for the long haul. It’s not for the short haul.” The company has also invested in its domestic manufacturing footprint. Reuss said GM has spent billions of dollars bringing supply chains, production capacity and final assembly back into the U.S., arguing that strengthening the country’s ability to manufacture vehicles and tech is important for its long-term competitive success. “The intent there is to bring industrial basis and might to our country with jobs and the power of making things and technology and everything that drives that,” Reuss explained. “And I’m all for that.” His one ask of Washington: a single national rulebook instead of state-by-state regulation. “You have no idea how many billions of dollars this industry has spent trying to satisfy individual state regulatory environments instead of a consistent countrywide set of regulations,” Reuss said. Demand for gas-powered engines, he added, “is still very high and has long tails to it.” This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Nvidia’s interim CEO Colette Kress takes on export compliance as Washington turns up pressure
events.summary: Nvidia’s national security and trade compliance teams will report directly to interim CEO Colette Kress and a new board oversight committee on day-to-day operations as the AI giant faces heightened scrutiny from Washington. Compliance has become a critical issue for Nvidia and  for Kress, who is also the company’s longtime finance chief, as questions swirl over the potential diversion of its advanced AI to China. The company said Tuesday that its board has formed a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee to oversee national security policies, export-control compliance and global trade risks. Suzanne Nora Johnson will chair the panel, joined by directors Stephen C. Neal and John O. Dabiri. The committee will meet at least quarterly and work with independent experts. Board Chair Harvey Jones said the committee would work to establish and advance a robust framework to “safeguard national security while supporting continued technological innovation.” The move comes amid heightened U.S. scrutiny of access to advanced AI chips. The Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security announced Monday an interim final rule addressing remote access to advanced computing technology through overseas data centers. The rule, developed at the direction of the Treasury Department and the National Security Council, aims to prevent companies in restricted countries from bypassing export controls by accessing computing power remotely through data centers in third countries. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has publicly criticized Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over the department’s handling of Megaspeed, a company suspected of facilitating the diversion of Nvidia AI chips to China. Megaspeed has also come under scrutiny following revelations about former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive whom U.S. authorities suspect of having ties to Chinese intelligence.  “Treasury, War, USTR, and State were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months,” Bessent told CNBC on Friday. “But Commerce has the pen.” The central export-control question is whether advanced Nvidia chips supplied through Megaspeed were diverted to China. U.S. rules have allowed certain data centers outside China to provide remote computing services to Chinese customers, but that is distinct from the unauthorized transfer of restricted physical chips, Fortune reported . On Sunday, Bessent further intensified scrutiny of Nvidia’s compliance practices, questioning whether potential violations of U.S. export restrictions were isolated incidents or reflected broader problems within the company. “I can tell you that if this were a bank and they hadn’t complied like this, the OCC [Office of the Comptroller of the Currency] would be in there right now and a lot of the executives would be removed,” Bessent said on Fox News’ Sunday Morning Futures . Nvidia’s 2026 proxy statement , published in May, says the company “does not have a chief compliance officer .” However, that does not mean it lacks a compliance structure. The proxy describes an enterprise risk management process reviewed by the CEO, other named executive officers reporting directly to the CEO, including Kress, Debora Shoquist, executive vice president of operations, and Timothy S. Teter, EVP, general counsel and secretary, as well as other senior management members. These leaders are responsible for managing and monitoring risks within their respective areas. Nvidia’s Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee also has explicit board-level oversight responsibility for trade compliance, regulatory matters and related risks, including issues at the center of the Megaspeed controversy. The five-member committee includes board chair Jones and is chaired by Neal. The newly established National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee adds another layer of board-level scrutiny, and puts export controls and national security risks firmly on the agenda as Nvidia navigates mounting pressure from Washington. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Google to keep Gemini chats for 2 months, up from 72 hours, even with history off
events.summary: Google is extending how long it keeps temporary Gemini chats and conversations made with chat history turned off to around two months, saying the change aims to improve safety and security as AI systems become more capable. The change , which will roll out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks, marks a significant increase from the previous 72-hour retention period mentioned in Google’s Gemini Apps Privacy Hub, according to an archived version from November 12. OpenAI, by comparison, says it may keep temporary chats in ChatGPT for up to 30 days, whereas Anthropic retains incognito chats in Claude for 30 days by default. However, companies may keep some data longer for legal or safety reasons, or to investigate policy violations. Google did not answer questions about what prompted the change and whether it would affect how conversations are accessed or reviewed, instead pointing to a blog post that says chats are kept longer to respond to users, process feedback, and protect its services and users. Its updated Gemini Apps Privacy Hub also cites potential system failures as a reason for retaining chats and says temporary conversations are not used to train AI models. The longer retention period comes as Google introduces separate settings for Gemini’s chat history and AI training. Until now, both were tied to a single “Keep Activity” setting. Users will now be able to keep their conversations in their chat history without using them to train Google’s generative AI models. Google says both new settings will be turned off by default for users who previously disabled Keep Activity. For those who had Keep Activity turned on, their chat history will remain enabled. events.title: Trump has a plan to limit student loans for nursing and other advanced degrees. A new bill would reverse those cuts.
events.summary: Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand co-led the introduction of a new bill to expand advanced degrees that qualify for a higher student-loan borrowing cap. Tierney L. Cross/Bloomberg via Getty Images A new bill calls to expand the list of programs that qualify for higher student-loan borrowing limits. Trump's repayment overhaul would allow 11 programs to qualify for the higher $200,000 borrowing cap. The bill calls for excluded programs, like advanced nursing, to qualify for the higher limit. Democratic lawmakers are pushing to expand access to higher student-loan borrowing limits . On Tuesday, Sens. Kirsten Gillibrand and Jeff Merkley introduced a bill that would expand the number of advanced degrees that qualify for a professional degree designation and thus a higher borrowing cap. President Donald Trump's student-loan repayment overhaul placed a $100,000 lifetime borrowing cap on graduate degrees and a $200,000 cap on professional degrees. The administration also planned to limit professional degrees to 11 programs, such as medicine and law, while excluding other programs like nursing, social work, and education. The limits were met with criticism by both Democratic and Republican lawmakers who argued that limiting borrowing for nurses would exacerbate the healthcare worker shortage. A lawsuit blocked the administration from implementing the new limits on July 1, and the Democratic lawmakers are now seeking to codify professional status for an expanded list of degrees . "Nurses, teachers, and social workers are dedicated public servants, and Congress must do everything it can to help recruit the next generation of these heroes," Merkley said in a statement. "We're already facing a shortage of these critical workers, and new limits on federal student loans for these professions and others threaten to further jeopardize the future of our workforce." The bill would maintain professional status for programs that already qualify while restoring professional status to additional programs, including nursing, public health, and physician assistant programs. It would also give the education secretary the flexibility to add more programs that meet the "professional degree" requirements. It follows a bipartisan bill earlier this year that called for the inclusion of advanced nursing degrees on the list of professional degrees, noting that tuition for some programs exceeded the borrowing cap. The Department of Education previously said that most advanced nursing programs borrow within the limits. After a blue wave in the midterms, Democratic lawmakers said they plan to bolster oversight of the student-loan industry and Trump's repayment changes through hearings, investigations, and legislation. Gillibrand said in a statement that students pursuing fields like social work or nursing "should not have to break the bank to serve their communities." "This bill would help our students, our universities, and our communities, and I'm determined to get it passed," she said. Have a story to share about student loans? events.title: Israeli settler pogrom kills Palestinian woman, wounds 10 people
events.summary: Will Israel’s election change life in Gaza? The Palestinian Health Ministry says Fadda Mohammed Fheidat, 72, was shot dead by Israeli settlers. Israeli settlers have killed an elderly Palestinian woman and wounded 10 other people in a pogrom in the central occupied West Bank, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. The Palestinian Health Ministry named the woman killed as Fadda Mohammed Fheidat, 72. list 1 of 3 Israeli court upholds detention of Palestinian land activist Ghassan Najjar list 2 of 3 Is Israel’s Eisenkot bloc less right wing than Netanyahu? list 3 of 3 Gunfire erupts in occupied West Bank settler attack The attack began early on Tuesday in the Duyuk al-Tahta neighbourhood on the outskirts of Jericho city, where settlers forcibly took over several properties earlier this month. Witnesses told the news agency Reuters that a group of settlers began shooting outside Fheidat’s home, and Palestinian residents threw stones to defend themselves. More settlers arrived and fired at Palestinian homes, including Fheidat’s, the witnesses said. Ahmed Aref, 62, Fheidat’s brother-in-law, said that a bullet hit her in the head as she stood in front of her house. “I found her lying on the ground, with blood coming from her head,” he said. The Israeli military did not comment on the woman’s death, but said it was dealing with “ongoing incidents” in which Israelis and Palestinians were wounded in an alleged car-ramming. Fheidat’s son, Arafat, rushed to the scene after hearing she was hurt. His wife, Naama Fheidat, said he was in shock and accidentally hit a settler’s car parked in the driveway. Witnesses said the settlers were not in the car, and that they then fired wildly, wounding several people, including Arafat, in the torso. Arafat Fheidat said the Israeli military stopped the ambulance he was in as he was being taken to hospital in Ramallah and arrested him. The military told Reuters a group of Palestinians in a car “accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it”, claiming that there were both Israeli and Palestinian casualties. The settler attack comes about two weeks after settlers took over eight homes in Duyuk al-Tahta, the official Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. The Binyamin Regional Council, which represents settlers in the area, said it had helped facilitate the move of families into eight homes purchased from Palestinians. Jericho’s Palestinian governor, Hussein Hamayel, has said the settlers could not legally buy the land because it belongs to the state. Israeli pogroms in the occupied West Bank have surged to what the United Nations has called an “unprecedented level”, following the Hamas-led attacks on southern Israel on October 7, 2023 and the subsequent genocidal war on Gaza. According to the UN, at least 1,143 Palestinians have been killed in the occupied West Bank since October 7, 2023, including 250 children. The figure includes Palestinians killed by Israeli settlers living in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank. The Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED) said 2026 is on track to be the most violent year for settler-related violence since it began monitoring the occupied West Bank a decade ago. In July alone, 11 people were killed in four incidents involving armed settlers alongside Israeli forces.

events.title: SBA chief defends policy barring green-card holders from loans, even if they can serve in U.S. military
events.summary: Small Business Administration chief Kelly Loeffler said Tuesday it’s “completely not true” that her agency’s new loan rules restrict immigrants. The rules she was defending bar green-card holders, who can legally work, pay taxes and, if otherwise eligible, enlist in the U.S. military, from SBA-backed loans. Under a policy that took effect March 1 , businesses must be wholly owned by U.S. citizens or nationals to qualify for SBA-backed loans, cutting out lawful permanent residents, commonly known as green-card holders, who were previously eligible. In fiscal 2025, the agency approved 3,358 loans to businesses partly owned by lawful permanent residents, about 4% of its 85,000 loan approvals, according to the SBA . Speaking at the Fortune 500 Innovation Forum in Detroit, Loeffler cast the rule as a question of who goes first: “Foreign nationals cannot get an SBA loan ahead of an American citizen.” “It strikes me as odd that we can send somebody to a battlefield on behalf of the United States,” Fortune Brainstorm Editorial Director Andrew Nusca told Loeffler. “We can take their taxes, but we can’t extend to them a loan.” “We have not yet run into a case where we’ve had to reject a veteran for that purpose,” Loeffler said. She didn’t directly address why green-card holders who serve in the military should be excluded. Instead, she pointed to the agency’s work supporting veterans, including a policy waiving down payments for eligible veteran entrepreneurs. Loeffler also argued that the SBA has limited funding and accounts for only a small share of the broader small-business lending market. Those excluded from its loan guarantees can still turn to banks, credit unions, venture capital firms and private lenders for financing, she said. The SBA generally doesn’t lend directly to businesses. Instead, it guarantees loans made by private lenders , helping eligible businesses obtain financing that might otherwise be difficult to secure.  Nearly half of Fortune 500 companies have immigrant roots America has roughly 36 million small businesses across America, but the country’s entrepreneurial success has long depended on immigrants. Nearly 46% of companies on the 2026 Fortune 500, or 229 businesses, were founded by immigrants or their children , according to the American Immigration Council. Together, those companies generated $9.8 trillion in revenue last year and employed 15.3 million people worldwide.  Nusca pointed to some of the country’s best-known business leaders, including Tesla’s Elon Musk, Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, AMD’s Lisa Su, and DoorDash’s Tony Xu, as examples of immigrant entrepreneurs who helped build major American companies. The immigration restrictions are among several changes Loeffler has made to the agency, which was established in 1953. Since taking office, she has reduced its workforce by more than half and announced plans to relocate field offices away from cities the administration designates as sanctuary jurisdictions.  Loeffler said the overhaul has made the agency more effective, citing $100 billion in capital backed over two years and efforts to move staff closer to growing small-business communities.  “Small business is big business,” she said. She also defended changes to the agency’s 8(a) Business Development Program , which supports socially and economically disadvantaged small businesses seeking federal contracts. Loeffler said the administration was tightening eligibility to ensure contracts reach businesses that qualify under the program’s rules.  Despite the agency’s shrinking workforce, she said about half of its loans last year went to businesses with fewer than 10 employees.  AI won’t replace workers, Loeffler says Loeffler also rejected the idea that artificial intelligence would necessarily displace small-business employees, arguing that labor shortages make automation increasingly valuable.  “This is a productivity tool. It’s not a job replacement tool,” she said. She pointed to manufacturers adopting robotics and automated equipment to handle jobs they struggle to fill, freeing existing employees to take on more skilled work. “We have prioritized lending to Americans because we have limited statutory availability of funding to go out to American citizens,” Loeffler said. This story was originally featured on Fortune.com

events.title: Microsoft Ignite 2026: Empowering human ambition, intelligence and trust
events.summary: November 17, 2026 Category: Company News Microsoft Ignite 2026: Empowering human ambition, intelligence and trust Microsoft Source | 5 minutes One year ago at Microsoft Ignite, we introduced Frontier Transformation. The premise was simple: technology exists to serve humanity and deliver real business outcomes. Over the course of this past year, we have been leading our customers to focus on the three durable traits that are required for successful transformation: human ambition, intelligence and trust. Ignite 2026 is the next milestone in this journey as we introduce new innovations that deliver on the promise of all three of these pillars. Our goal is to build a frontier ecosystem , one that lets every organization benefit from progress at the frontier while preserving what makes it unique.   “We need to parlay any technological advance into real outcomes and new points of leverage for people, organizations and society at large,” said Satya Nadella, Microsoft Chairman and CEO, in his opening keynote at Ignite. “For us, that comes down to three things: keeping human ambition at the center, ensuring you have ownership over your organization’s intelligence and learning, and trust.” Human ambition: AI should serve humanity, not the other way around It starts with the work people are trying to do, which is why we think of Microsoft Copilot as the new operating system for work.   New Copilot Workspaces gives people and agents a shared space to work together as a team. Autopilot, a long-running agent, can manage recurring tasks and move projects forward without being prompted at every step, and Copilot Code lets anyone build dashboards, trackers and apps in natural language with enterprise security and governance built in. Together with Office in Copilot, and features like Today, they make up the new Copilot, which is built to translate raw intelligence into real value. Copilot is already driving transformation at scale among our customers. Volkswagen Group is equipping more than 330,000 employees with Copilot and The Estée Lauder Companies has expanded Copilot to more than 14,000 people across its global workforce. Copilot is also connecting to the systems teams rely on most, including Dynamics 365, as well as announcing Salesforce in Copilot , a plugin available in preview with more than 38 pre-built sales skills. Intelligence: Compound your intelligence without giving away your IP Agents are only as effective as the context they work with. Microsoft IQ is the enterprise context management platform that helps organizations build their own IQ by capturing, governing and reusing the business knowledge apps and agents need. New business plugins let teams package that knowledge into reusable, trusted context, skills and tools that can be shared across the business.  Customers are already turning that intelligence into business outcomes. Publicis Groupe is empowering employees to build custom AI skills that combine Microsoft IQ with Publicis’ industry expertise and proprietary data, then test them against real-world client scenarios. The result is faster innovation, quicker decision-making and greater value for clients. In Microsoft Foundry , new continuous improvement tools help customers develop more powerful agents and even train models automatically based on real production signals: optimizing for quality, latency and cost-effectiveness. New models for coding, cyber image and audio are also being introduced, as well as the general availability of Microsoft-Decision-1.1 , a fast, low-cost decision model for tasks like routing, classification, prioritization, verification and workflow control. Trust: Observability at every layer of the stack and for every person As agents move from answering questions to taking action, trust becomes the deciding factor. There should never be a choice between innovation and safety. Microsoft Perception , now generally available, brings together specialized agents to find, defend and remediate vulnerabilities — powered by models including our MAI-Cyber line — to help defenders stop threats at machine speed. Agent 365 Business Analytics gives leaders a clear view of what their AI is costing and what it is delivering, from task success to hours assisted. And Windows is expanding its operating-system-level protection for agents, with more granular containment with Microsoft Execution Containers, built-in agent identity with Entra support and Agent 365 policies enforced on every device, giving IT more control over agent activity in their organizations. Building on its use of Microsoft Defender, Entra and Purview, BNY is exploring capabilities in Project Perception to further strengthen security and governance. These efforts support BNY’s broader AI ambitions, including its collaboration with Microsoft to complete the first agentic negotiation of a U.S. Treasury trade. Infrastructure: A cloud built for AI at global scale Microsoft builds Azure as a single system, co-designing silicon, servers, networking and racks around what we learn running workloads at scale. As agents increasingly work outside the model, from running tools to compiling code, CPUs matter even more. Cobalt 200 virtual machines , generally available today, deliver up to 50% better performance than the previous generation. Cobalt will reach 23 regions by year end and becomes a significant share of new Azure compute capacity in 2027. Azure Catalyst brings Azure and GitHub agentic tools together in one connected experience for modernizing the applications, databases and infrastructure that AI depends on, and hybrid intelligence on Windows lets AI run wherever it makes the most sense, on the device or in the cloud, starting with GitHub Copilot for coding and Copilot for everyday work. Taken together, today’s announcements demonstrate that the organizations that pull ahead in this next phase are the ones that connect intelligence to their people, their data and their processes, with trust built in from the start. That is the frontier ecosystem we are building with our customers and partners. To see it in action, watch the Microsoft Ignite keynote and explore the full set of announcements in the Book of News .
